newsitem.title: UK: European stocks off highs awaiting Wall St open.
newsitem.headline: European stocks off highs awaiting Wall St open.

text.p: A strong early recovery in European stock markets slowed by mid-morning on Monday as investors awaited Wall Street's opening for further direction.
Traders said stocks had tracked Asian markets higher after a slide on Friday sparked by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's comments about "irrational exuberance" on world financial markets.
But nervousness following Friday's slide and domestic factors were seen keeping a lid on gains, at least until Wall Street offered fresh evidence that Friday's late bounce from lows was sustainable.
British, German and French shares were all off highs by mid-morning, and traders said they would take direction from Wall Street later in the day.
U.S. shares in London offered an early indication that stocks would extend their recovery, but volumes were low.
"No one is rushing in to snap up bargains just yet. This market is tricky and could easily come off again," one dealer said.

A 1.6 percent bounce in the Nikkei-225 index in Tokyo set the tone for European stocks, which were aided by comments by Bank of England governor Eddie George and U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin that markets overreacted on Friday to Greenspan.
Greenspan's remarks raised concern about a possible tightening in U.S. monetary policy, which boosted the dollar on Monday morning.
Traders said further major losses were unlikely in the short term.
"Generally the optimism seems to be hardening that we are not at the start of some sort of meltdown and the Far Eastern markets were OK," a head of equity sales in London said.
In London, the FTSE 100 index gained over 40 points at one stage but was capped by talk of an early election following the latest outbreak of tensions in the ruling Conservative Party.
The FTSE 100 was 27.3 points higher at 3,990.3 at 1123 GMT after ending Friday 88.2 points off at 3,963.0 -- its biggest one-day loss in percentage terms since February 1994.
German shares rushed ahead after Friday's dive as a firmer dollar and Bunds lent support. Analysts and traders said the market's upward trend was intact, and viewed Friday's fall as an overreaction.
"I am totally bullish. The market had the weekend to digest what happened last week and is in far calmer form," said on Munich dealer.
The DAX index was up 61.7 points at 2,853.66 at 1124 GMT, a 2.2 percent rise from Friday's close. It earlier touched 2,872.57.

French shares ran out of steam and gave back some of their opening gains ahead of the start of trading on Wall Street, dealers said. December CAC-40 futures halved their opening gains, which were booked in a rebound from Friday's 2.26 percent fall in the CAC-40.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 11.86 points at 2,253.22 at 1127 GMT.
Dutch shares opened firmer as the feeling grew that Friday's fall was overdone.
The AEX index was 5.26 points up at 621.52, against an early high of 624.28.
Most other European markets were moving ahead cautiously after Friday's losses.
